reason: Start with the filter to follow what leaves the blood before useful substances are recovered.
expectation: Small substances, including glucose and waste, should pass through while blood cells and large proteins stay in the blood.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the route to the bladder, but I want to follow filtering first.

effect: The filter lets useful glucose and water through along with wastes, so the recovery tube is the next part to follow.
reaction: It was interesting that filtering doesn't just separate out waste.
reason: Use the recovery tube to follow useful substances back toward the blood.
expectation: Glucose, some salts and much of the water will return toward the blood, leaving fluid with wastes behind.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the route to the bladder, but I want to finish following the filtered fluid first.

effect: Useful substances and much water return to blood, leaving waste-containing fluid to collect in the bladder.
reaction: It makes sense why the recovery step matters after filtering.
reason: Add the ureters to start the route from the kidneys to the bladder.
expectation: The ureters will connect to the kidney outlets, with the bladder still to add.

alternatives.reason: The bladder also needs fitting, but the ureters follow the route outward from the kidneys.

effect: The ureters now connect to the kidney outlets, leaving the bladder to complete the route.
reason: Fit the bladder to complete the drainage route; it's the only offered combination.
expectation: The ureters will connect the kidneys to the bladder, where urine can collect.

effect: The ureters now connect the kidneys to the bladder, providing a route for urine to collect.
reaction: The continuous route makes the parts easier to understand.
reason: Follow the remaining fluid into the completed drainage route before connecting the organs to the body.
expectation: The waste-containing fluid will travel through the ureters and collect as urine in the bladder.

alternatives.reason: Connecting the organs to the body also advances a goal, but I want to follow the fluid first.

effect: The remaining fluid reaches the bladder as urine while blood continues through a separate vessel.
reaction: The separate routes make the result clear.
reason: Connect the urinary organs to the body; this is the only offered combination and completes the remaining goal.
expectation: The kidneys, ureters and bladder will be placed in the body, with the kidneys connected to the blood supply.

effect: The urinary organs are now connected to the body and its blood supply, completing the chapter.
reaction: The final picture clearly connects the blood and urine routes.

mostWorthwhile.text: Filtering the blood and then recovering useful substances was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidneys don't just remove waste in one step.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bladder was clear but predictable, especially as it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: I was surprised that glucose and water pass through the filter along with wastes and must be recovered.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the ureters and bladder had clear roles in the drainage route.

continue.text: I'd choose to continue: following the filter, recovery tube and drainage route made the kidney's job understandable, though the final fittings were predictable.
